baseline_models.focus_anchor: The opposed conditions in "when God is called alone, you reject" and "if a partner is assigned to Him, you believe."
baseline_models.mechanism: The invocation's configuration acts as a trust test: an unshared divine claim triggers covering and refusal, whereas a shared arrangement supplies the audience with security and assent. The problem is therefore not absence of belief as such, but belief switching on when authority is distributed.

activation_trace.role: Calling and inclining by speech supplies the summons whose configuration tests the hearers.
Unity without partner supplies the deliberately unshared pole of the test.
Covering supplies a material image for suppressing the sole claim rather than merely lacking information.
A stake shared among partners supplies the arrangement that makes assent acceptable.
Security and trust make "believe" an affective reliance response, not only a proposition.

changed_reading.before: The ayah contrasts monotheism with polytheism.
changed_reading.after: The ayah diagnoses a trust switch: the audience rejects an undivided claim yet feels able to assent when agency and liability appear shareable.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The result clause "so judgment belongs to God, the High, the Great."
baseline_models.mechanism: After the audience tries to allocate a divine share, the result clause reserves both restraint and adjudication to God. Highness as mastery and greatness as rightful majesty remove that jurisdiction from the peer scale on which partners could be added.

activation_trace.role: Restraint that checks corruption makes judgment the brake on the audience's attempted allocation.
Adjudication between parties supplies the exclusive jurisdiction asserted by the clause.
Mastery and prevailing power place the judge above every proposed co-holder.
Rightful majesty supplies a greatness that cannot be partitioned among rival claimants.

changed_reading.before: The closing names say that God will judge and is exalted.
changed_reading.after: The close actively voids the hearers' allocation scheme: the restraining and deciding jurisdiction remains with the One whose mastery is outside partner comparison.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive constructions "God is called" and "a partner is assigned," followed by the exclusive ownership of judgment.
baseline_models.mechanism: The call can be heard not only as prayer but as advancing a claim or entitlement. On that branch, the audience rejects the sole claim, endorses a shared claim, and is then told who alone has authority to validate claims.

activation_trace.role: Claiming a right or affiliation lets the invocation function as a claim advanced for God.
Shared ownership supplies the rival proposal to divide that claim.
Heart-settling assent is the audience's endorsement of the divided proposal.
Delegated arbitration raises the question of who was ever authorized to validate the proposed shares.

changed_reading.before: The ayah reports two opposite worship reactions.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it stages competing entitlement claims and closes by denying that the audience can authorize or arbitrate a share in divinity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated command to call God while purifying din turns "alone" from a bare number into an operation: mixed allegiance is cleared of added shares, and obedience is handed over without residue.

activation_trace.role: No-partner unity remains the focus anchor whose practical form the context supplies.
Purification after admixture supplies the removal process implicit in calling God alone.
Exclusive singling apart from partnership makes the removed admixture specifically a rival share.
Obedience and yielding identify what is being purified, not merely the wording of a prayer.
Handing over and releasing control supplies the positive transfer that follows removal of rival allegiances.

structural_cues: 40:66 places worship of those called besides God against the command to submit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated call-purify-din language and images of purification, exclusive singling, obedience, and transfer; I infer that "alone" demands clearing mixed allegiance. A live alternative limits ikhlas to inward sincerity without a social or juridical transfer.

changed_reading.before: Calling God alone means mentioning only one deity.
changed_reading.after: Calling God alone is a de-mixing act that clears obedience of co-claims and transfers allegiance without a retained share.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah tests ownership of judgment by efficacy: God decides in truth, invoked alternatives decide nothing, His decided command becomes, and the final arrival of His command enacts judgment. Exclusive judgment is therefore operative jurisdiction, not a title.

activation_trace.role: Adjudication supplies the focus claim that the context subjects to an efficacy test.
Cutting judgment marks both God's true decision and the called alternatives' inability to decide anything.
The same calling relation identifies the alternatives whose jurisdiction fails.
Perfecting and executing an act supplies the causal force of the decided matter.
Binding command supplies the content that becomes effective with "Be."
The decisive judgment with truth supplies the public enactment of the focus clause.
Actual loss supplies the measurable consequence of failed rival jurisdiction.

structural_cues: 40:20 directly contrasts God's judging with the non-judging of those called besides Him.
40:68 and 40:78 move from decision to effective command and final adjudication.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit decision contrasts, an executed command, and final loss; I infer that efficacy is the criterion by which the focus reserves judgment to God. A live alternative keeps creative command and courtroom judgment as separate domains.

changed_reading.before: Judgment belongs to God as a future verdict.
changed_reading.after: Judgment belongs to God because His decisions alone cut, execute, and produce consequences; the invoked partners fail the jurisdiction test in the present.

context_deltas.mechanism: The believing man's dialogue makes calling bidirectional recruitment: he calls his people toward rescue, they call him toward fire by demanding rejection and partnership, and their object is denied any valid call or claim. The focus reaction belongs to a contested summons network.

activation_trace.role: A claimed right or affiliation anchors the exploratory claim dimension in the focus call.
Opposed verbal summonses supply reciprocal recruitment toward rescue and fire.
Shared participation supplies the concrete demand carried by the counter-summons.
The denied call or claim strips the rival object of entitlement in both worlds.

structural_cues: 40:41-42 reverse "I call you" and "you call me" before naming rejection and partnership.
40:43 says the object of their invitation has no call in either world.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reciprocal summonses, an explicit partnership demand, and denial of the rival's da'wah; I infer that invitation and entitlement reinforce each other. A live alternative reads da'wah throughout only as invitation or prayer, without a legal claim sense.

changed_reading.before: The focus call is an isolated act of invocation.
changed_reading.after: The focus call sits inside rival recruitment and claim-making: assent to partnership is participation in a counter-summons whose object has no valid entitlement.

context_deltas.mechanism: Followers ask their former superiors to absorb or offset an allotted share of punishment, but the superiors cannot suffice and answer that God has already judged. Partnership-based trust is exposed as imagined risk pooling: shared authority promised distributed liability, yet no patron can carry another's portion.

activation_trace.role: Shared stakes anchor the focus arrangement that is tested as a liability network.
Security and reliance identify why a distributed arrangement could attract belief.
Binding liability in followership supplies the obligation the followers try to transfer upward.
Sufficiency supplies the patrons' tested and failed ability to cover their followers.
An assigned share supplies the portion of liability the followers ask others to absorb.
God's completed adjudication terminates every attempted redistribution among patrons and followers.
The redirected request to the keepers extends the failed chain of delegated calling.

structural_cues: 40:47-48 stages followers, arrogant leaders, an allotted portion, failed sufficiency, and God's judgment in one exchange.
40:49-50 continues with another delegated call that produces no relief.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies followership liability, an allotted share, failed sufficiency, and final judgment; I infer that the focus audience trusts partnership partly as risk distribution. A live alternative treats the scene as generic failed patronage without explaining the earlier attraction of partnership.

changed_reading.before: Belief in partners is a mistaken inventory of divine beings.
changed_reading.after: Belief in partners is also reliance on a distributed responsibility system whose patrons are expected to absorb risk but cannot alter a single judged share.

context_deltas.mechanism: Pharaoh converts inner self-magnification into a high structure and an attempted route of attainment and inspection. The focus names "the High, the Great" then distinguish divine mastery from both built altitude and greatness manufactured in the chest but never reached.

activation_trace.role: Prevailing mastery anchors highness as authority rather than merely physical elevation.
Rightful majesty anchors the scale against which human self-magnification is exposed.
The high building supplies Pharaoh's fabricated vertical substitute for divine highness.
Reaching a limit supplies the attempted conversion of height into access.
A rope or connection supplies the imagined means linking the tower to the divine domain.
Overlooking and uncovering supply Pharaoh's attempt to inspect and master what exceeds him.
The chest as the source of action locates the rival vertical project internally before it becomes public.
Human pride supplies the counterfeit greatness driving dispute.
Failure to reach the sought limit explicitly denies that counterfeit greatness its goal.

structural_cues: 40:35 joins disputation, magnified loathing, a sealed arrogant heart, and coercion immediately before the tower project.
40:56 relocates the same kibr to the chest and says its possessors will not attain it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a high structure, connective means, attempted attainment, inspection, inner kibr, and non-attainment; I infer that the focus titles deconstruct fabricated vertical sovereignty. A live alternative treats the tower episode as ridicule of Pharaoh without making it a calibration of "High, Great."

changed_reading.after: They deny that sovereignty can be reached by built altitude or produced by self-enlargement: divine highness is mastery, while the rival height begins as unattainable kibr in the chest.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command "Call Me; I respond to you" reverses the focus response direction: God answers the undivided call, while humans who reject it are identified as self-magnifying against worship and end abased. The true call is a reciprocal circuit broken by counterfeit greatness.

activation_trace.role: The focus summons anchors the human response side of the circuit.
Rightful divine greatness anchors the contrast with human self-magnification.
The direct call supplies the input to God's promised response.
Submissive worship identifies the relation from which the rejecters magnify themselves.
Self-arrogation of greatness supplies the blockage in the call-response circuit.
Abasement supplies the terminal reversal of claimed human greatness.

structural_cues: 40:60 places call, divine response, arrogance from worship, and abasement in one causal sequence.
The focus likewise places call, human rejection, and the divine title "Great" in one sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies God's promised answer and the arrogance-to-abasement sequence; I infer a reciprocal circuit in which the focus records the human side failing. A live alternative limits "I respond" to granting petitions rather than a broader reciprocity of recognition.

changed_reading.before: The focus only asks how humans respond when God is invoked.
changed_reading.after: The undivided call opens a two-way response: God answers, but self-magnifying humans refuse worship; "the Great" names the rightful pole that their pride counterfeits.

context_deltas.mechanism: At the surah's end the focus polarity reverses almost word for word: after seeing overwhelming force, they believe in God alone and disavow what they had partnered. The next ayah says that this sight-triggered faith no longer benefits, making judgment a response deadline rather than only a verdict.

activation_trace.role: Denial of the sole claim supplies the initial polarity that the ending reverses.
No-partner unity supplies the initially rejected object.
Association with God supplies the initially accepted object.
Heart-settling assent supplies the response whose object and timing change.
Direct sight supplies the new evidentiary threshold that triggers reversal.
Overwhelming force supplies the coercive object of that sight.
Assent now moves to God rather than to the partnered arrangement.
God without partner becomes the now-confessed object.
Disavowal and renunciation reverse kufr's object from God-alone to the former partners.
The former association is explicitly named as what they now renounce.
Failure of benefit marks the reversed response as pragmatically too late.
A recurrent governing course turns the failed late reversal into a stable response rule.

structural_cues: 40:84 repeats belief, God alone, rejection, and partnership in the opposite alignment from 40:12.
40:85 repeats sight of force and faith, then explicitly denies that faith benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact lexical reversal and ties it to sight of force and non-benefit; I infer that the decisive difference is the response threshold, with compelled recognition arriving after judgment becomes visible. A live alternative grounds the failure of late faith in a rule other than coercive timing.

changed_reading.before: The focus describes a fixed identity: rejecters of God-alone are believers in partnership.
changed_reading.after: It captures an earlier phase in a reversible polarity: judgment eventually flips both belief and rejection, but a sight-compelled flip arrives after responsive faith can benefit.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-root material analogy, not a derivation or claim that kufr and forgiveness are lexically identical. It remains anchored in the focus's covering branch and in the surah's repeated protective-covering branch for forgiveness; downstream prose should render it as a contrast in the object and effect of covering.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the human act that hides the sole divine claim.
A covering that protects supplies the divine counter-image announced at the surah's opening.
Covering sin and shielding its bearer from effect supplies the requested protective direction.
The Forgiver appears as the destination of the believer's rival call, keeping protective covering inside the call contest.

changed_reading.before: Kufr in the focus is simply rejection.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the surah contrasts two coverings: humans cover the sole claim to suppress it, while God covers sin to protect its bearer; judgment distinguishes concealment from preservation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The hunter's-snare branch of shirk is branch-distant and must not replace the ordinary partnership sense. It remains anchored in the focus root and is activated by the immediate chain-dragging scene before the partners are questioned; downstream prose should present it only as a materialized image of entanglement.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus passive "if a partner is assigned to Him."

activation_trace.role: A hunter's snare supplies an exploratory entanglement image inside the focus root.
A collar binding the limb materializes restraint around the neck.
Connected links supply the extended binding mechanism.
Dragging and extending supplies the motion imposed by the binding.
The direct question about their divine partners reconnects the restraint scene to the ordinary focus sense.

changed_reading.before: Partnership is an additive belief that gives the audience reassurance.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the added relation is also a snare: the trusted network becomes visible at judgment as linked restraint and involuntary dragging.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation shifts the social effect of "alone" from its grammatical referent, God, to the human confessor, so it must not be presented as the syntax of 40:12. It remains worth carrying because the surah places concealed individual faith inside parties and later exposes follower loyalty; downstream prose should qualify it as a social consequence of exclusive allegiance.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The collision between "God alone" and the shared-stake branch of partnership.

activation_trace.role: Separation and being without a companion supplies the social cost potentially radiating from exclusive allegiance.
Shared participation supplies the socially populated alternative.
A party gathered around one view supplies the coalition environment in which calls are heard.
Concealing faith supplies evidence that exclusive allegiance can isolate its bearer within the ruling household.
Trust borne by the concealed believer supplies the costly alternative to coalition-backed security.
Loyal following supplies the social attachment that partnership-like authority preserves until it fails.

changed_reading.before: The audience prefers more than one divine object.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the audience also prefers the coalition security of shared allegiance; confessing God alone can leave the confessor socially alone, as the concealed believer's position makes visible.

strongest_changes: The focus antithesis became a trust-distribution mechanism: undivided authority triggers covering, while shared stakes offer apparent security.
The surah expands calling into rival recruitment, entitlement, and reciprocal response, not merely an isolated prayer formula.
Exclusive judgment became effective jurisdiction, tested by the partners' inability to decide, execute, or redistribute liability.
40:84-85 reverses the focus polarity almost word for word and shows that sight-compelled faith arrives after it can benefit.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly reactivated the exact focus roots in juridical, social, vertical, material, and temporal scenes, allowing several mechanisms to coexist without collapsing them into one doctrinal paraphrase.
remaining_uncertainties: The claim-entitlement branch of da'wah may be activated chiefly by 40:43 rather than already active in the focus.
The risk-pooling and social-isolation models are coherent narrative mechanisms but remain inferential rather than syntactically stated.
The counter-covering and partner-snare images are cross-root or branch-distant and should remain explicitly exploratory.
